title: Opportunistic host staging and proactive-restart orchestrator for throughput-safe upgrades
creator: Mira Chen
description:
Problem: During node lifecycle events (OS/kernel patches, driver updates, and planned restarts) we observe tail latency spikes and transient throughput drops on Dedicated pools when many hosts are taken out of service concurrently. Existing drain workflows are conservative and cause long maintenance windows or require heavy manual coordination across capacity slices.

Goal: Implement an "opportunistic host staging and proactive-restart orchestrator" that minimizes SLO perturbation by: 1) staging replacement hosts ahead of retire/drain events, 2) prewiring prefix/KV warmup and model cache preheating before traffic shifts, 3) performing coordinated micro-restarts with throughput hedging and short-lived traffic siphons, and 4) exposing configuration primitives for throughput reservation and autoscaler interaction. The feature should be pluggable into Dedicated autoscaling and maintenance pipelines and provide observable guarantees for per-tenant throughput during upgrades.

Design summary:
- Staging pool: create a transient staging pool in each availability slice. Staging hosts join serving behind a warmup state where kernel selection, model artifacts, and tokenizer caches are preloaded. Staging hosts report a readiness score based on KV cache hit estimates, GPU memory compaction, and model kernel JIT completion.
- Traffic handoff: use a two-step handoff: (a) siphon a small shadow % of traffic to staged hosts to validate correctness and measure latency/throughput; (b) if validation passes, incrementally shift weight while maintaining a configured throughput hedging band (e.g., maintain 85-95% of baseline throughput on the originating hosts while shift completes).
- Proactive-restart choreography: instead of draining hosts immediately, run a timed restart phase that evicts long-lived connections and gracefully rebinds short-lived requests via ephemeral routing shards. Restarts are limited by concurrent-restart caps per slice to limit impact.
- Autoscaler interplay: staged hosts are created using a short-lived reservation quota that does not immediately trigger permanent capacity billing; autoscaler policies will be extended with a new "maintenance-reservation" mode that treats staged hosts as hedges rather than backfill capacity.
- SLO/guardrails: operators can set per-fleet throughput guarantees, a max-concurrent-restarts value, and a baseline window for acceptable latency regressions. The orchestrator will abort and rollback if throughput falls below the configured hedging band for longer than a threshold.

APIs and config:
- New maintenance profile: maintenance_profile{staging=true, warmup_timeout=60s, concurrency_limit=2, hedging_band_low=0.85, hedging_band_high=0.98, prewarm_artifacts=[modelA:v3, tokenizer:v2]}
- Observable signals: staged_readiness_score, siphon_error_rate, on_path_throughput_pct, proactive_restart_progress.

Telemetry & alerts: add dashboards showing prewarm latency, staged readiness distribution, throughput during handoff, rollback frequency, and per-tenant impact. Alert if rollback > 2 per week per fleet or if hedging band violations exceed 1%.

Rollout plan: alpha with internal Dedicated fleets in us-west1, monitor for 2 weeks, then gradual beta with a small set of customer tenants who opt in. Coordinate with Support & SRE runbooks for manual abort and postmortem playbooks.

Artifacts & links: 1) Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/REINF/Opportunistic+Host+Staging 2) Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4519 3) Early dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/maintenance/opportunistic-staging

Security/compliance: no new customer data plane flows. All staged hosts run existing encryption/KMS integrations. No PII exposure expected.
comments: 2025-02-26 - Kickoff: Aligning with Runtime and Autoscale teams. Identified model artifact download as the primary contributor to warmup latency.

2025-03-01 - Prototype results: Staged readiness score stabilized after ~42s for Llama-2-13B-v2 with kernel JIT disabled; with JIT enabled warmup spikes but final readiness is higher. Need to capture JIT completion signal in readiness score.

2025-03-02 - Design review notes (from Jorge Ramos): Prefer explicit prewarm artifact lists to avoid implicit large downloads during staging. Also suggested a capped network egress budget for staging to avoid noisy neighbor effects.

2025-03-03 - Trade-off decision: We will implement hedging band enforcement in the control plane to allow immediate rollback rather than relying on operators to notice regressions. This increases control plane complexity but reduces customer impact risk.
2025-03-04 - QA checklist added: integration tests for staged readiness scoring, canary siphon validation, rollback trigger on hedging band violation, autoscaler reservation timeout recovery.

2025-03-05 - Blocker discovered: some Dedicated fleets with aggressive local caching bypass readiness signals due to mismatched cache key prefixes. Follow-up task ENG-100512 opened to standardize cache prefixing across fleet variants.
